text.p: British property company Greycoat Plc rejected a rescue approach from its smaller rival Moorfield Estates, describing the proposal as "vague as to value."

In a statement Michael Beckett, chairman of Greycoat, said "We have received an outline proposal from Moorfield. It contains no new ideas, fails to place a value on Greycoat, lacks a cash alternative and does not enhance shareholder value."
"At this stage we do not propose to take these discussions any further," he added.

Moorfield's management also has "little experience of central London office investment or development," said the company. Greycoat is being urged by UK Active Value Fund, which owns 11 percent of the company, to liquidate its 500 million stg property portfolio.

Moorfield, capitalised at about 45 million stg, suggested that it make a share exchange offer for Greycoat, which is capitalised at 185 million, at an unquantified restated asset value, said Greycoat.
It is then proposing to split the enlarged group into two separate companies.
